entities.summary: Abd al-Salam's revolt was an early 19th century uprising against the Sokoto Caliphate led by Abd al-Salam of Kware, a Ba-Are Hausa scholar and one of the principal disciples of Shehu Usman dan Fodio, founder of the Caliphate. Taking place between 1817 and 1818, soon after Usman's death, the revolt was among the most serious internal challenges faced by his successor, Muhammad Bello.
